page.title:
Open source.
Open possibilities.
page.description: Ubuntu brings open source to your desktop, data centre and cloud. A familiar platform for everyday work, professional development and enterprise infrastructure.
page.body:
One platform, from the workstation to the cloud
Ubuntu is a modern, open source operating system for desktops, servers and connected devices. On the desktop, it brings together applications for browsing, communication and content creation with the libraries and toolchains developers need. On the server, the same foundation supports databases, web applications, containers and cloud infrastructure. Teams can develop on a laptop and deploy to production without leaving the Ubuntu ecosystem.

Security that grows with your needs
Long term support releases provide a stable foundation for organisations planning beyond the next upgrade. Ubuntu Pro adds expanded security maintenance, kernel live patching and tools for hardening and compliance. Whether you are setting up a personal workstation or managing a fleet of servers, you can choose the maintenance and support that fit the workload. Ubuntu remains free to download, use and share.

page.title: Ubuntu for desktops
page.description: The open source operating system powering millions of PCs and laptops around the world. Built for everyday work, professional developers and enterprise environments.
page.body:
Everything you need for the everyday
Ubuntu offers applications for web browsing, messaging, gaming and content creation. Work with familiar tools such as Firefox, Chrome, Discord, Steam and OBS Studio, alongside thousands of applications available through the wider Ubuntu ecosystem. Use your desktop for writing, collaborating and creating, with the freedom to choose the tools that suit the way you work.

A platform for professional developers
Each release of Ubuntu delivers applications, libraries and toolchains for modern development. Ubuntu is a platform for major integrated development environments, game development tools and AI and machine learning software. Develop locally with familiar Linux tools, then move your work to Ubuntu Server or a cloud environment without having to learn a different operating system.

Private, secure and ready for the enterprise
Regular updates and built-in security features help protect the operating system and the applications you rely on. Ubuntu also integrates with enterprise environments. For organisations with additional requirements, Ubuntu Pro provides security patching, fleet management options and tools for hardening and compliance, while retaining the same familiar desktop experience.

Open source, from the start
Ubuntu has always been free to download, use and share. Its development depends on a worldwide community of contributors working alongside Canonical. That open foundation gives individuals and organisations the freedom to inspect, adapt and build on the software, rather than treating the operating system as a closed box.

page.title: Ubuntu Server
page.description: Secure, scalable Linux for your data centre, public cloud and private cloud. A lean foundation for applications, containers and infrastructure at any scale.
page.body:
Scale out with Ubuntu Server
Ubuntu Server brings technical scalability to enterprise data centres and public or private clouds. It supports a broad range of workloads, from web services and databases to OpenStack clouds and Kubernetes clusters. A lean initial installation lets teams start with what they need, then add the services and tools required by their applications as demand grows.

Performance and versatility
Ubuntu Server is certified by leading hardware manufacturers and includes tools for deployment and application management. The same platform can support a small application server, a database fleet or a larger cloud environment. This consistency helps teams reuse their Linux skills, automation and operational practices rather than maintaining a different foundation for every workload.

A release schedule you can plan around
Long term support releases receive standard security updates for packages in the Ubuntu Main repository for five years. Interim releases arrive every six months for teams that want access to newer features. Hardware enablement updates bring support for newer machines to supported LTS releases, helping organisations balance a stable software base with changing infrastructure requirements.

A maintenance path for your fleet
Ubuntu Pro adds tools for hardening, compliance, kernel live patching and expanded security maintenance. It extends security coverage beyond the standard maintenance period and into more of the open source packages used by applications. Organisations can choose additional support services when they need help operating or troubleshooting their infrastructure.

page.title: Ubuntu on campus
page.description: An illustrative university deployment, using Ubuntu Desktop for teaching labs, software development and everyday productivity. This is a fictional case study.
page.body:
The challenge: one lab, many ways of working
In this fictional scenario, a university needs a desktop environment for programming courses, group projects and everyday study. Students move between web-based learning tools, office applications, development environments and command-line utilities. The IT team wants a consistent platform that students can also install on their own computers, without introducing a separate operating system for each course.

A desktop for learning and development
Ubuntu Desktop combines applications for browsing, communication and content creation with the libraries and toolchains used by professional developers. Students can work with familiar browsers and integrated development environments, while learning the Linux tools they will encounter on servers and in the cloud. Ubuntu is free to download, use and share, making it possible to carry the same environment beyond the teaching lab.

Keeping the environment manageable
An LTS release gives the university a stable base for its lab image, while regular security updates support day-to-day operation. For labs with additional maintenance or compliance requirements, Ubuntu Pro offers expanded security coverage and management options. The choice of maintenance services can be made separately from the choice of applications used in each course.

The intended result
A shared desktop foundation can make it easier to prepare teaching materials and reproduce development environments across university and personal machines. This example illustrates capabilities described on Ubuntu.com; it does not report a real university deployment, measured savings or customer endorsement.

page.title: A cloud for research
page.description: A fictional research team uses Ubuntu Server and OpenStack to give researchers a shared, self-service computing environment.
page.body:
The challenge: from individual machines to shared resources
In this illustrative scenario, a research group has outgrown a collection of individually managed workstations. Different projects need virtual machines, storage and isolated environments for experiments. The group wants researchers to request resources when they need them, while keeping a consistent operating system underneath its applications and infrastructure.

A familiar Ubuntu foundation
Ubuntu Server supports infrastructure workloads such as databases, containers and private clouds. Researchers who already develop on Ubuntu Desktop can use familiar Linux tools when moving their work to server environments. Long term support releases provide a stable base for shared infrastructure, with a maintenance schedule that can be considered alongside the lifespan of research projects.

Self-service infrastructure with OpenStack
OpenStack provides programmable APIs and a self-service portal for provisioning and managing cloud resources. Its open source foundation brings code transparency, while components such as KVM, Ceph and OVN provide virtualisation, storage and networking. Integration with Kubernetes and support for a range of hardware make it relevant to both traditional and cloud-native applications.

The intended result
The team aims to spend less effort configuring individual machines and more time running its research workloads. The architecture is based on Ubuntu Server and OpenStack capabilities described on Ubuntu.com. The organisation, project and outcome here are fictional; no performance, cost saving or production deployment is claimed.

page.title: Ubuntu Desktop or Server?
page.description: The same open source foundation, with different starting points. Choose for the person at the keyboard, the services in your infrastructure, or both.
page.body:
Choose Desktop for the person using the machine
Ubuntu Desktop provides a graphical working environment for PCs and laptops. It brings together applications for web browsing, communication and content creation, alongside the tools used for software development. It is a natural starting point for people who spend their day working directly with applications, writing code or collaborating with others on a personal computer.

Choose Server for the workload
Ubuntu Server is a lean foundation for infrastructure and services. It is designed for environments such as data centres, public clouds and private clouds, supporting workloads from web applications and databases to Kubernetes and OpenStack. Administrators can build the system around the required services, using remote access, deployment tools and automation rather than relying on a desktop interface.

Use the same skills across both
Desktop and Server share the Ubuntu ecosystem, package management and Linux tools. A developer can build and test locally before deploying to an Ubuntu server or cloud environment. That does not make a laptop and a production system identical, but it gives teams a familiar foundation for documentation, scripts and operational knowledge.

Plan maintenance separately from the interface
Both editions offer long term support releases. Ubuntu Pro adds expanded security maintenance and other capabilities for desktop and server systems. The decision is therefore not simply which edition has more features: start with how the machine will be used, then choose the maintenance, security and support options appropriate to that use.

page.title: Ubuntu LTS and Ubuntu Pro
page.description: Ubuntu LTS provides a stable foundation. Ubuntu Pro adds expanded security maintenance, live patching and tools for organisations with longer-term requirements.
page.body:
What comes with Ubuntu LTS
An Ubuntu long term support release provides five years of standard security maintenance for packages in the Main repository. It gives individuals and organisations a predictable base for desktops, servers and applications. For many systems, that combination of a stable release and regular security updates is the right starting point.

What Ubuntu Pro adds
Ubuntu Pro extends security maintenance to ten years for the Main and Universe repositories, covering more of the open source software used in infrastructure and applications. Ubuntu.com describes coverage across the operating system and application stack, including components such as PostgreSQL, OpenSSL, PHP and Redis. An optional Legacy add-on can extend the maintenance period by another five years.

Security operations beyond individual updates
The subscription also includes kernel Livepatch and tools for auditing, patching automation and hardening. Compliance profiles support organisations working with security standards. These capabilities help teams plan how they will maintain a fleet, not just how they will install the next package update. Additional support options are available for organisations that need operational assistance.

Build on the Ubuntu you already run
Existing Ubuntu LTS systems can be upgraded to Ubuntu Pro in place, without redeploying the operating system. Ubuntu Pro is free for personal use on up to five machines, while organisations can evaluate enterprise options. The account and subscription shown in this demo remain fictional; this page is a product comparison, not a purchase or activation flow.

post.title: Open source, from the desktop to the cloud
post.description: Build on your laptop, run services in the data centre, and scale into the cloud with a familiar Ubuntu foundation.
post.body:
Start where the work happens
Ubuntu Desktop brings together everyday applications and the tools used by professional developers. The same machine can be used for browsing, collaboration, writing code and testing a new service. With access to libraries, toolchains and development environments, a project can begin on a familiar desktop rather than requiring a separate infrastructure environment for its first steps.

Take the workload into production
Ubuntu Server provides a foundation for the infrastructure behind that project. It supports services such as web applications and databases, as well as container and cloud platforms. Long term support releases give teams a stable base and a predictable maintenance window. Skills learned on a development machine remain useful when working with an Ubuntu server, even as operational requirements become more demanding.

Build a cloud on open infrastructure
OpenStack combines virtualisation, storage and networking with programmable APIs and self-service resource management. Ubuntu.com describes it as a platform for both traditional workloads and modern cloud-native applications. Combined with an Ubuntu foundation, it gives teams another way to place workloads where their infrastructure, governance and operational needs make sense.

Keep the freedom to build
Ubuntu is free to download, use and share. Its open source development model brings together Canonical and a global community of contributors. For teams moving between desktops, servers and clouds, the value is not that every environment is identical: it is the ability to build on familiar tools and an open foundation as their needs evolve.

post.title: A little more peace of mind with Ubuntu Pro
post.description: Expanded security maintenance, kernel Livepatch and hardening tools, without replacing the Ubuntu LTS systems you already run.
post.body:
Look beyond the base operating system
An application depends on more than its operating system kernel. Databases, language runtimes and libraries all contribute to the software that an organisation needs to maintain. Ubuntu Pro extends security coverage into the Main and Universe repositories, helping teams consider more of their open source application stack when planning long-term maintenance.

Plan for a longer service life
Ubuntu Pro extends the maintenance horizon of Ubuntu LTS from five years of standard security maintenance for Main to ten years across Main and Universe. The optional Legacy add-on offers another five years. A longer maintenance window can help organisations plan migrations around the needs of an application, rather than treating every system as a short-lived installation.

Make security part of operations
Kernel Livepatch, auditing and patching automation support the work of keeping systems maintained. Hardening tools and compliance profiles help organisations apply security requirements consistently. These capabilities complement the updates themselves: teams still need an operational plan for their machines, applications and responsibilities.

Start with your existing Ubuntu systems
Ubuntu Pro can be added to an existing Ubuntu LTS system without redeploying it. Personal use is free on up to five machines, and enterprise evaluation and support options are available. The dashboard in this demonstration shows a fictional account and sample machines so that the private account experience can be explored separately from public product content.
